physical_mismatches.reason: The source model is a lumped single-node RC circuit for one uniprocessor. It has no floorplan, block geometry, spatial heat spreading or per-block power map, so a spatial 2D or 3D chip thermal model cannot reproduce it.

The paper gives no 3D stack, interposer or chiplet structure. Package thermal resistance is only a lumped scalar (R = 22 C/W) taken from vendor data. Cooling and heat-sink details are not described beyond this.

The source result is a transient closed-loop experiment. It combines runtime ambient-temperature estimation, DVFS switching, task-period adaptation and idle-time insertion, with temperature-dependent leakage in the model. A steady-state or open-loop Studio run does not reproduce this controller.

The optimizer and controller (LP parameter assignment, EDF idle-time scheduler, RT-MTC feedback baseline) are real-time OS scheduling mechanisms. A chip thermal solver has no equivalent, so they are not replicated.

Power is given only as total-processor quantities (Pmax = 3860 mW, activity factors, average task powers in Fig. 2). No per-block power rows are published, and total power must not be split without a published rule.
No reliability or lifetime metric is evaluated. Only the Tmax = 60 C constraint and the percentage of time it is violated are used.

studio_assumptions: No pinned packet assets are supplied, so no Studio package or material assumptions are recorded. None are asserted as matching the paper.
Any Studio run would be a separate illustrative construction that is not paper-derived. Its coordinates and temperatures must not be compared numerically to the paper's 59.6 C.
